Marginal Radon–Nikodym (MRN) identification weights

Source: R/weights.R
dot-marg_rn_weights.Rd

Per-unit marginal Radon–Nikodym weights \(\alpha_{ij}(\phi_c)\) (Theorem all_weights / Prop. weights (i)) for the two counterfactual regimes. The weights marginalise over the within-cluster assignment of each neighbouring cluster, so a unit contributes whenever its cluster neighbourhood has positive probability under both regimes.

Usage

.marg_rn_weights(
  A,
  C,
  W_C,
  W_Y,
  dist1 = "binom",
  params1 = list(prob = 0.5),
  dist0 = "binom",
  params0 = list(prob = 0),
  distC = "binom",
  paramsC = list(prob = 0.7),
  unit_weights = NULL
)

Arguments

A

n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix (with self-loops).

C

integer vector of cluster ids.

W_C

0/1 vector of cluster-level treatments, indexed by cluster id.

W_Y

0/1 vector of individual-level treatments.

dist1, params1

within-cluster assignment law of the treated regime phi_1.

dist0, params0

within-cluster assignment law of the control regime phi_0.

distC, paramsC

cluster-level assignment law.

unit_weights

optional per-unit weights (default: uniform); only units with nonzero weight are processed.

Value

A list with numeric vectors weights1 and weights0.

Examples

set.seed(1)
A <- Matrix::Matrix(outer(1:12, 1:12, function(i, j) abs(i - j) <= 1) * 1,
                    sparse = TRUE)
C <- rep(1:3, each = 4)
W_C <- c(1, 0, 1)
W_Y <- rbinom(12, 1, ifelse(W_C[C] == 1, 0.5, 0.2))
w <- generalClusterExp:::.marg_rn_weights(A, C, W_C, W_Y,
  dist1 = "binom", params1 = list(prob = 0.5),
  dist0 = "binom", params0 = list(prob = 0.2),
  distC = "binom", paramsC = list(prob = 0.7))
cbind(phi1 = w$weights1, phi0 = w$weights0)
#>            phi1      phi0
#>  [1,] 0.6811989 1.7438692
#>  [2,] 0.9928515 1.0166799
#>  [3,] 1.2873326 0.3295572
#>  [4,] 1.1329647 0.2900390
#>  [5,] 1.3671661 0.3499945
#>  [6,] 1.2873326 0.3295572
#>  [7,] 1.2873326 0.3295572
#>  [8,] 1.3671661 0.3499945
#>  [9,] 0.9500646 0.9728662
#> [10,] 0.9928515 1.0166799
#> [11,] 0.5184571 2.1236002
#> [12,] 0.6811989 1.7438692
